title: A new smallest item arrives
hook: The smallest item must always sit on top. Must you re-sort everything to keep it there?

knows: a tree as parents and children
doesNotKnow: how a min-heap keeps its smallest item on top cheaply
that a heap can be stored as an array

misconception: To keep the smallest item on top after each insert you must re-sort everything.
objective: The learner can explain that inserting into a min-heap puts the item at the end and swaps it with its parent while smaller, so [2, 5, 3, 9, 6] plus 1 becomes [1, 5, 2, 9, 6, 3] after 2 swaps, and an insert costs at most the tree's height, about log2 n swaps.

claims.text: In a min-heap every parent is smaller than (or equal to) its children, so the smallest item is on top.
claims.source: Cormen et al., Introduction to Algorithms (3rd ed.), 6.1 (min-heap property A[PARENT(i)] <= A[i]). The stage says 'smaller'; all values here are distinct.

claims.text: Inserting 1 into [2, 5, 3, 9, 6]: 1 swaps with 3 (index 5 to 2), then with 2 (index 2 to 0), giving [1, 5, 2, 9, 6, 3]. 5, 9 and 6 never move.
claims.source: Demo.tsx FINAL, computed with the same bubble() the stage uses (parent of i = floor((i - 1) / 2)); builder re-ran the swaps in Node.

claims.text: Each swap climbs one level, so an insert costs at most the tree's height, about log2 n swaps: 2 for 6 items, at most 19 for a million.
claims.source: CLRS 6.1 (height of an n-element heap is floor(log2 n)) and 6.5 (MIN-HEAP-INSERT / HEAP-DECREASE-KEY run in O(log n)). floor(log2 6) = 2, floor(log2 1,000,000) = 19 (computed in Node).

claims.text: A heap can be stored as an array where the parent of index i is (i − 1)/2 rounded down.
claims.source: Zero-based layout; CLRS 6.1 uses one-based PARENT(i) = floor(i / 2), equivalent after shifting indices.

recall.question: A min-heap holds 1,000 items. You insert a new item smaller than all of them. About how many swaps does it take to reach the top?
recall.why: It climbs one level per swap, and a 1,001-item heap is floor(log2 1,001) = 9 levels tall, so at most 9 swaps.
